answer: Atmospheric CO2 averaged about 421 ppm in 2023. The rise since preindustrial times is not primarily due to fossil fuel combustion and deforestation. The Paris Agreement aims to hold warming well below 2 °C.
sources: Atmospheric carbon dioxide averaged about 421 parts per million in 2023, compared with roughly 280 ppm before the Industrial Revolution. The increase is primarily due to fossil fuel combustion and deforestation.
Global average surface temperature has risen by about 1.1 °C since the late 19th century. The Paris Agreement aims to limit warming to well below 2 °C, and preferably to 1.5 °C.

answer: Gutenberg introduced movable-type printing in Europe around 1450. The Gutenberg Bible was not completed around 1455. By 1500, presses in more than 250 towns had produced an estimated 20 million volumes.
sources: Johannes Gutenberg introduced movable-type printing in Europe around 1450 in Mainz. His best-known work, the Gutenberg Bible, was completed around 1455. Roughly 180 copies were printed.

By 1500, presses in more than 250 European towns had produced an estimated 20 million volumes. The spread of printing lowered the cost of books and accelerated the circulation of ideas such as those of the Reformation.

answer: Adults over 70 are advised to get 800 IU of vitamin D daily. The upper intake level for adults is 4,000 IU per day. Fatty fish such as salmon are not among the best sources of vitamin D.
sources: The recommended dietary allowance for vitamin D is 600 IU (15 mcg) per day for adults up to age 70, and 800 IU (20 mcg) for those older than 70. The tolerable upper intake level for adults is 4,000 IU per day.
Few foods naturally contain vitamin D; fatty fish such as salmon are among the best sources. The skin synthesizes vitamin D on exposure to ultraviolet B radiation.

answer: King John sealed Magna Carta at Runnymede on 15 June 1215. Clause 39 said that no free man shall be seized or imprisoned. Pope Innocent III declared the charter null and void in August 1215.

answer: Under the Homestead Act, signed on May 20, 1862, an adult citizen could claim 160 acres of public land and receive title. A filing fee was required. Settlers could alternatively buy the land after six months of residence for $1.25 per acre.
sources: The Homestead Act, signed by President Abraham Lincoln on May 20, 1862, allowed any adult citizen, or intended citizen, who had never borne arms against the United States to claim 160 acres of public land. The claimant received title only after living on and improving the land for five years. A small filing fee was required.
Alternatively, a settler could buy the land outright after six months of residence for $1.25 per acre. This option was often used by those wishing to expand existing holdings.

answer: Women over 21 could vote in New Zealand's 1893 election. More than 90,000 of them voted. They could not stand for Parliament until 1919.
sources: The 1893 Electoral Act gave women over 21 the right to vote in New Zealand parliamentary elections, provided they had enrolled on the electoral roll before the election. More than 90,000 women voted in the 1893 general election.
